Power Energy Transportation Biotechnology Pharmaceutical & Chemicals Heavy Engineering Electrical & Electronics Mining Minerals Oil & Gas Aviation Maintenance Services Petroleum Refining Marine Cement General Manufacturing Logistics and Procurement Procurement and logistics are the starting point of the supply chain, involving the sourcing, storage, and movement of essential materials. Logistics experts help reduce costs by optimizing transportation and procurement processes, ensuring smooth operations and greater efficiency. Logistics and Supply Chain Management Think of Supply Chain Management (SCM) as the recipe, and logistics as just one ingredient. While both focus on moving goods from origin to destination, SCM provides the overall strategy for sourcing, production, and delivery. Logistics ensures that everything arrives at the right place, at the right time—executing the plan SCM creates. Logistics and Inventory Management A key part of supply chain management, logistics and inventory management involves planning the movement and storage of goods to ensure timely, accurate delivery to customers. Larger organizations often face greater challenges, requiring precise control to maintain optimal stock levels. This prevents mismatches and ensures consistent customer satisfaction. Shipping and Logistics Management Shipping refers to the physical movement of goods, while logistics ensures that the entire process runs smoothly. Logistics encompasses everything from planning routes to coordinating deliveries—ensuring shipments are efficient, timely, and cost-effective. For example, food delivery services rely on strong logistics systems to get meals to customers fresh and on time. Transportation Management in Logistics Transportation management focuses on planning and executing the most cost-effective movement of goods. It can operate internally or through a third-party logistics provider (3PL) for outsourced fulfillment. As a key part of supply chain management, it covers all types of freight—domestic, international, inbound, and outbound. Effective transportation logistics requires strategic planning and smart procurement to ensure timely and efficient delivery. Distribution and Logistics Management Logistics focuses on planning and organizing the movement of goods, while distribution deals with their physical delivery and placement. Though distinct, both functions work together to enhance supply chain efficiency. They also align with related activities like warehousing and inventory control—ensuring products reach the right place, at the right time, and at the lowest possible cost.
